newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia's Lanes to merge with Barlow unit.
newsitem.headline: Australia's Lanes to merge with Barlow unit.

text.p: Australia's Lanes Ltd said itS Bristol Paints unit will merge with Taubmans Pty Ltd, which operates the Taubmans decorative and architectural paint business in Australia, through Lanes acquiring Taubmans from South Africa's Barlow Ltd.
Lanes will pay for the acquisition by the issue of 8.90 million new Lanes shares at an issue price of A$3.28 per share, it said.
The consideration represents a purchase price of A$29.19 million which is equal to the estimated net assets of Taubmans as at completion, it said.
Lanes said that in addition, Barlow had entered into an agreement with Lanes' shareholder Thorney Pty Ltd to acquire 4.62 million Lanes shares from Thorney at A$3.28 a share.
Thorney will retain two million Lanes shares.
Including the new Lanes shares that Barlow will be issued for acquisition of the Taubmans business, Barlow will own 44 percent of Lanes' expanded issued capital, Lanes said.
Further, Lanes will issue 3.76 million options to Barlow, exercisable at any time for a period of three years from completion date, to give Barlow up to 50.1 percent of Lanes.
However, to the extent Barlow acquires shares on market, options will be cancelled, Lanes said.
The exercise price of the options is A$3.28 plus an escalation rate of 80 percent on each anniversary of the completion date.
In a separate statement, the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCC) said it was unlikely to intervene in the proposed merger of Taubmans and Bristol Paints.
"The proposed merger of Taubmans and Bristol may prove beneficial for competition in the paint Industry," ACCC chairman Allen Fels said.
"Paint users may well benefit from this merger through vigorous competition between three major paint manufacturers."

"The ACCC decided it is unlikely to intervene based on the information it collected during the aborted acquisition by Wattyl of Taubmans in 1996. But we reserve our usual rights in making inquiries now the merger is public," he said.
In May 1996, the ACCC refused to authorise Wattyl Ltd's proposed acquisition of Taubmans on the ground it would have been anti-competitive.
Lanes said the merged Bristol-Taubmans group would have an estimated 22 percent of the Australian decorative paint market.
